title: Partially Linear Autoencoders for Manifold Learning and Dimensionality Reduction
abstract: arXiv:2608.29867v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Autoencoders are widely used for nonlinear dimensionality reduction and manifold learning. While most common implementations rely on both nonlinear encoders and decoders, we investigate the specific role of the encoder and the extent to which it can be constrained to be linear without reducing accuracy. We conduct a comparative study on four autoencoder architectures: standard fully nonlinear autoencoders (AE), linear-encoder autoencoders (Lenc-AE), linear-decoder autoencoders (Ldec-AE), and fully linear autoencoders (LAE), evaluated on synthetic manifolds, computational mechanics data sets, and real-world image data sets including MNIST. We demonstrate that imposing a linear encoder preserves most of the representational capacity of the autoencoder, provided the decoder remains nonlinear. tldr: 该论文通过对比四种自编码器架构，发现只要解码器保持非线性，将编码器约束为线性即可保留自编码器的大部分表示能力，其重构质量可媲美全非线性自编码器并显著优于线性解码器和全线性架构。
en_tdlr: Constraining the encoder of an autoencoder to be linear while keeping a nonlinear decoder preserves most of its representational capacity, with linear-encoder autoencoders achieving reconstruction quality comparable to fully nonlinear AEs and consistently outperforming linear-decoder and fully linear variants.
